stem: A subset of stored containers develops an unusual odor while the rest of the batch appears normal. Which response best preserves quality-control evidence?
choices: Separate the suspect containers from sale, document their storage history, and compare them with unaffected containers before deciding disposition.
Quarantine the suspect subset, preserve lot traceability, investigate moisture/storage/contamination factors, and apply defined release criteria.
Retain the entire batch together while increasing routine inspection frequency so no containers are treated differently during the investigation.
Shift the investigation toward upstream cultivation inputs first because storage-related odor differences are usually established before packaging.
rationale: Segregation, traceability, and investigation preserve evidence and reduce the risk of releasing potentially compromised material.
